name: Streamline Moderne
places: United States (Depression-era civic and transport design)
garments: not primarily a fashion look — an industrial and architectural design style

media.title: Raymond Loewy's industrial design (Coldspot refrigerator, 1935; locomotives)

reacts_against: Art Deco's ornamental geometry, stripping it down to smooth, curved, wind-tunnel-inspired forms that implied speed even on a stationary building or toaster.

wiki_facts.other_names: Art Moderne, Streamline Design, Style Paquebot
wiki_facts.key_motifs: Curved corners, horizontal lines ("speed lines"), smooth and unadorned surfaces, glass block, chrome accents, porthole windows
wiki_facts.key_colours: Often white or pale earth tones, with accents of chrome and steel
wiki_facts.key_values: Speed, efficiency, modernity, technology, motion, functionality

findings: mostly muted — about 71% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from the Aesthetics Wiki images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
